images.title: Multiples of 5
images.purpose: Show that multiples of 5 always end in 0 or 5.
images.composition: One evenly spaced row of 4 square tiles, one label centred below, lots of white space.
images.exact_structure: One row of 4 equal squares evenly spaced, holding 5, 10, 15, 20. Each square has a teal #0072B2 outline, and its last digit is drawn in reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 4 squares, 5 labels.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a last digit coloured differently from the others
images.takeaway: The last digit of a multiple of 5 is 0 or 5.
images.description: Four tiles showing 5, 10, 15 and 20 with each last digit highlighted.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the highlighted digit in each tile and say what repeats.

image_decisions.why: The last digit pattern of a short row of multiples is the one idea.
